1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls required()/getSession() and derives the account id solely from the server-side session record (s.userId), never from client-supplied identifiers.

2.why: Verification material is per-account (TOTP secret encrypted per user record, recovery codes as per-user PBKDF2 verifiers) and the code is checked against the session's own account state, so cross-user reuse does not hold — although the identity step uses a hardcoded constant IDENTITY_CODE in this single-account fixture.

3.why: Session rotation only occurs at /api/signin and /api/identity; confirm() sets m.enabled = true without invalidating any other existing sessions, so concurrently established sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext (encrypt/encryptedSecret) and recovery codes only as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 (120k iteration) verifiers, never plaintext.

5.why: All session ids, CSRF tokens, nonces, TOTP seeds and recovery codes come from bytes()/crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and the session cookie is HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, though test-mode secrets/OTPs are held in JS variables, printed to console and rendered into the DOM.

7.why: Server enforces JSON content-type, strict key allow-listing, length truncation and regexes for email, phone, 6-digit codes and recovery-code format; there is no SQL layer at all.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with textContent/createElement (never innerHTML), and a nonce-based CSP with base-uri 'none' and frame-ancestors 'none' is applied.

9.why: The only redirect input is validated with b.redirect !== "/" (an exact internal allow-list of one) and no Location-based redirect is ever issued.

10.why: headers() sets Content-Security-Policy (incl. frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and Referrer-Policy on every response.

11.why: cookie() and expired() both emit mfa_session with Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Errors are generic ("Request could not be completed.") with no stack traces, but TEST_MODE = true returns testIdentityCode, testProvisioningSecret, testAuthenticatorCode and plaintext recoveryCodes in API responses which the client then console.logs and renders into a visible log panel.

13.why: The identity code is marked identityUsed and expires after CODE_LIFE (5 min), TOTP is accepted only within the live 30-second period, and a matched recovery code is spliced out inside the account lock.

14.why: addFail()/MAX=5 with a 10-minute LOCK window is applied to identity codes, TOTP confirmation and recovery-code verification, with checks of identityLocked/authLocked/recoveryLocked before validating.

15.why: A brand-new session id is issued (old one deleted) on sign-in and on identity verification, getSession() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
